headline: Women-only 'Pink Buses' launched in Dhaka, Chattogram and Bogura
summary: The BRTC has introduced a dedicated bus service for women to ensure safer travel, with plans to expand the service to every district across Bangladesh.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has launched a new 'Pink Bus' service specifically for women in three major cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura.
The service was officially inaugurated by the Road Transport and Bridges Minister, aiming to provide women with a safer and more comfortable commuting experience.
The government intends to expand this women-only bus service to every district in the country to improve accessibility and mobility for female passengers.
However, the launch was marred by an incident on the first day where a Balaka bus collided with one of the new Pink buses.
The initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance safety and security for women using public transport in Bangladesh.
caption:
A safer commute for women? BRTC launches 'Pink Buses' in three major cities.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has launched a new 'Pink Bus' service specifically for women in three major cities: Dhaka, Chattogram, and Bogura.

The service was officially inaugurated by the Road Transport and Bridges Minister, aiming to provide women with a safer and more comfortable commuting experience.

The government intends to expand this women-only bus service to every district in the country to improve accessibility and mobility for female passengers.

However, the launch was marred by an incident on the first day where a Balaka bus collided with one of the new Pink buses.

The initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance safety and security for women using public transport in Bangladesh.

headline_marked: 1,472 AI cameras installed on Dhaka-Chattogram highway to [[curb highway extortion]]
headline: 1,472 AI cameras installed on Dhaka-Chattogram highway to curb highway extortion
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an AI-powered 'Auto Fine System' to reduce illegal tolls and improve traffic law enforcement.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an AI-powered 'Auto Fine System' on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, featuring 1,472 AI cameras.
The system is designed to automatically detect traffic violations and issue fines, reducing the need for manual intervention by officers on the road.
The Home Minister stated that the implementation of AI cameras will significantly help in curbing highway extortion and illegal tolls collected from transport vehicles.
He further announced that this AI auto-fine system will eventually be introduced on all major highways across Bangladesh to ensure transparency and safety.
The move is expected to modernize traffic management and reduce the corruption associated with manual traffic stops and fines.
caption:
1,472 AI cameras are now watching the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to stop illegal tolls.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an AI-powered 'Auto Fine System' on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, featuring 1,472 AI cameras.

The system is designed to automatically detect traffic violations and issue fines, reducing the need for manual intervention by officers on the road.

The Home Minister stated that the implementation of AI cameras will significantly help in curbing highway extortion and illegal tolls collected from transport vehicles.

He further announced that this AI auto-fine system will eventually be introduced on all major highways across Bangladesh to ensure transparency and safety.

The move is expected to modernize traffic management and reduce the corruption associated with manual traffic stops and fines.
